sections.label: Budget cut for Head F
sections.summary: A motion is moved to reduce the total sum allocated for Head F of the Estimates by $100.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head F of the Estimates be reduced by $100." Singapore has come a long way since independence and much of our progress will be was built on the bedrock of political stability.

sections.label: Cooling off periods proposed
sections.summary: A step is to introduce cooling off periods between partisan and non-partisan roles so individuals can detach from previous associations.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A step is to introduce cooling off periods between partisan and non-partisan roles, allowing individuals to meaningfully detach from previous associations.

sections.label: Cooling-off periods in other jurisdictions
sections.summary: The UK and Canada impose cooling-off periods barring Ministers, backbenchers and senior civil servants from private entities or lobbying.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Jurisdictions from the United Kingdom (UK) to Canada impose various cooling-off periods, prohibiting Ministers, backbenchers and senior civil servants from joining private entities or undertaking lobbying activities to better manage potential revolving door conflicts of interest, along with the risk of undermining public trust, or even the perception of regulatory capture.

sections.label: Scrutinising PA budget and partisanship
sections.summary: Grassroots advisors may extend a ruling party's machinery, so the taxpayer-funded PA budget should be scrutinised.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: If grassroots advisors are an extension of a ruling party's political machinery, then we should be candid.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And relatedly, we should scrutinise the PA budget, which is provided by taxpayers with these considerations, particularly when it shapes whether Members of this House are able to access the state resources that they come with.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Ultimately, this will ensure that our institutions uphold the principles of a parliamentary democracy where the will of the people is respected.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It would be a shame if the lack of clarity of whether something is partisan or not, takes us back to the days when voters were threatened to have public funds withdrawn, upgrading pushed back should they not make the right choice.

sections.label: Parliamentarians acting with integrity
sections.summary: Democracies are safe only when Parliamentarians act honourably and accept accountability for their responsibilities and conduct.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Democracies can only be safe when the Parliamentarians, in whose hands democracy is entrusted, act honourably and with integrity and who, when things go wrong, have the courage and the sense of shame to accept accountability for matters within their responsibility, and their personal conduct.

sections.label: Resigning WP to become NMP
sections.summary: If she resigned from the WP and declared it, nothing stops her becoming an NMP the next day if selected.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The answer is, if she resigned from the WP and declared that, there is no obstacle to her becoming an NMP the following day, provided that when she, assuming she is selected, carries out those duties as an NMP properly.

sections.label: Grassroots advisor versus MP roles
sections.summary: The speaker says the point is wrongly filed under this cut and was answered by Minister Ong Ye Kung, who explained the difference between grassroots advisor and MP roles.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: So, first, it is wrongly filed under this cut.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: So, I do not propose to address it in detail, other than to say that this has been answered quite fully by Minister Ong Ye Kung in a separate earlier session of Parliament, where he explained the difference between the role of a grassroots advisor, which is essentially flowing from Government, and that of an MP.

sections.label: Singapore political leadership ideals
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore's system resembles the British system, with Singaporeans adding the ideal of upright, trustworthy leaders of ability and integrity committed to the public good.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Singapore system is more like the British system, except as Mr Goh noted, Singaporeans have gone further and super-imposed on our constitutional framework, the ideal of a political leader who is upright, morally beyond reproach, someone people can trust and we believe that leaders must be men and women of ability and integrity, committed to the public good.

sections.label: Cooling-off, conflicts, WP disciplinary matter
sections.summary: The speaker cites a three-year corporate governance cooling-off, the Minister on conflicts of interest, and clarifies the WP disciplinary matter and the Motion's many limbs.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: The first is, I heard the Minister's explanation earlier about how as long as you tell people that you have stepped down from your partisan role or your non-partisan role, and you are switching over to the other side.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: But I think I quoted earlier that there is a code of corporate governance which has a three-year cooling off.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: And then the second point, I believe, was the Minister saying about conflicts of interest.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: I just wanted to set the record straight that even though some of the WP MPs were tasked by the WP Central Executive Committee to look into the matter of our Secretary-General, Mr Pritam Singh, this was an internal party disciplinary matter.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: I do not want to pre-empt nor speak for the panel at this stage.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: But also just to clarify that the Motion that was tabled before Parliament was on many limbs.
